full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 251

Sichuan Mou Chemical Co., Ltd. v. Shandong Mou Chemical Co., Ltd., et al. — enforcement implementation case

(Approved by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on April 7, 2025)

Keywords: enforcement; enforcement implementation; intellectual property; elevated enforcement; enforcement settlement

Key Points of Enforcement Implementation

1. In enforcement cases involving acts, where circumstances exist such as the person subject to enforcement continuing to commit the infringing acts involved, multiple significant cross-regional related cases, and the need for coordination by a higher people's court, resulting in the case not being concluded within six months from the date of filing for enforcement, the higher people's court may adopt measures such as elevated enforcement or supervisory enforcement to promote the case's execution.

2. For enforcement cases involving acts such as dismantling production equipment that infringes intellectual property, the people's court, while fully protecting the legitimate rights and interests of the right holder, may guide both parties to reach a settlement, replacing the dismantling of relevant production equipment with the person subject to enforcement paying technology license fees, thereby promoting the lawful use of such production equipment and achieving a win-win or multi-win outcome.

Basic Facts

In the dispute over infringement of technical secrets between Sichuan Mou Chemical Co., Ltd. and Shandong Mou Chemical Co., Ltd., et al., the Supreme People's Court rendered a civil judgment on December 26, 2022, (2022) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Min Zhong No. 541: Shandong Mou Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shandong Mou Chemical Company) and others were ordered to immediately cease selling melamine products manufactured using the technical secrets involved owned by Sichuan Mou Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sichuan Mou Chemical Company), destroy the equipment involved in the project (including but not limited to dismantling the parts of the relevant equipment containing the technical secrets involved) and the technical secret materials held, and jointly and severally compensate Sichuan Mou Chemical Company for economic losses and reasonable expenses totaling RMB 98,000,000 (currency unit: RMB). Because Shandong Mou Chemical Company failed to perform the obligations under the effective judgment within the prescribed time limit, Sichuan Mou Chemical Company applied for compulsory enforcement.

This case was enforced by the Tianfu New Area People's Court of Sichuan Province. During the enforcement process, after online asset investigation and garnishment, the monetary obligations were fully enforced, but the obligations to cease selling infringing products and destroy infringing equipment and technical materials as determined in the judgment were not voluntarily performed by the person subject to enforcement. Moreover, destroying the involved production equipment was extremely difficult: the equipment involved tens of thousands of fine parts, making it hard to precisely determine the scope of dismantling; the equipment was flammable and explosive, and improper operation could cause serious chemical pollution; there were very few domestic companies with relevant dismantling qualifications, and there was no precedent for similar dismantling operations; the equipment was located in another province, requiring cross-regional coordination. At the same time, there were three related cases between the applicant for enforcement and the person subject to enforcement pending at the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province and the Sichuan High People's Court, all arising from the infringing acts involved in this case. The behavioral obligations determined by the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court's judgment were identical to those in this case, and the person subject to enforcement had not performed them; the subject matter of the two cases pending before the Sichuan High People's Court was as high as RMB 600,000,000.

In December 2023, the Supreme People's Court decided to supervise this case, directing and coordinating the compulsory enforcement measures and enforcement progress milestones, and led a special meeting to study enforcement plans including elevated enforcement, and in accordance with the obligations determined in the effective judgment and the special circumstances of this case, guided the parties to reach a settlement, clarifying the work approach of "package resolution" of the four related cases between the parties in Sichuan and Guangdong. Subsequently, the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province lawfully elevated enforcement of this case. The Sichuan High People's Court, Chengdu Intermediate People's Court, together with the Guangdong High People's Court, Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court, Shandong High People's Court, the intermediate people's court of the location of the person subject to enforcement, and relevant Shandong departments, held multiple seminars to guide the parties to finally reach an enforcement settlement agreement whose main contents included the person subject to enforcement paying technology license fees, infringement compensation, and continued production and operation using the equipment involved.

Enforcement Result

On January 28, 2024, Sichuan Mou Chemical Company and Shandong Mou Chemical Company reached a settlement and signed an agreement to "resolve in a package" this case, one case filed for enforcement by the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court, and two cases pending before the Sichuan High People's Court. In August 2024, Shandong Mou Chemical Company remitted the full amount of RMB 440,000,000 specified in the settlement agreement to the account designated by the applicant for enforcement. The Chengdu Intermediate People's Court issued a notice on August 28, 2024, (2023) Chuan 01 Zhi No. 4918, concluding this case.

Enforcement Reasoning

This case is a difficult and complex case involving behavioral enforcement in the field of intellectual property. Choosing appropriate enforcement methods and strategies to guide and facilitate an enforcement settlement, promoting the "package resolution" of disputes, and achieving a win-win or multi-win outcome were key to handling this case lawfully and properly.

First, regarding the enforcement method. Pursuant to Article 237 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, where a people's court fails to enforce within six months from the date of receiving the application for enforcement, depending on the specific circumstances of the case, the higher people's court may order the original people's court to enforce within a time limit, or may designate another people's court in its jurisdiction to enforce, or directly elevate the case for enforcement by itself. According to Article 74, paragraph 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Execution Work of the People's Courts (For Trial Implementation) (Fa Shi [1998] No. 15, revised in 2020), "Where a lower court has failed to conclude a case for a long period and it is truly necessary, the higher court may decide to execute the case by itself, jointly with the lower court, or designate another court in its jurisdiction to execute." In this case, there were three other significant related cases between the applicant for enforcement and the person subject to enforcement in Guangdong and Sichuan, and the applicant expressed to the court its wish to resolve all disputes in an integrated manner. Moreover, both the person subject to enforcement and the infringing equipment were located in other provinces, and compulsory dismantling of the involved production equipment required high professional expertise, had no domestic precedent, and posed significant safety risks. Therefore, relying solely on the original enforcement court to conduct cross-province and cross-department coordination was evidently difficult and could not guarantee enforcement efficiency and effectiveness. It was necessary to adopt elevated enforcement and other measures to facilitate smooth and efficient case handling.

Second, regarding enforcement measures. The civil judgment serving as the enforcement basis, (2022) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Min Zhong No. 541, clearly stated that destroying the relevant equipment included but was not limited to dismantling. Given the specific circumstances of this case, simply and directly adopting compulsory enforcement measures was not the optimal solution. The involved equipment was flammable and explosive, requiring highly specialized dismantling; improper operation could cause serious chemical pollution. Forcibly dismantling the involved equipment would make it difficult for the enterprise to continue production and operations, and would affect related industrial chains, impacting the enterprise's survival, employee employment, and local economic development. Conversely, the involved production equipment had the capacity for sustainable production and was not outdated capacity requiring elimination. If licensed, it could continue to be used lawfully, maximizing the utility of the property. This would protect the survival of the infringing enterprise, safeguard employee employment, and maximize the interests of the intellectual property rights holder, achieving better economic and social benefits. Furthermore, by paying infringement compensation and technology license fees for continued use, thereby obtaining lawful authorization to use the relevant technical equipment, the judgment's requirements and the purpose of rights protection could also be achieved. This is an enforcement measure that deserves particular attention in technology-related intellectual property infringement cases. Accordingly, the people's court strengthened coordination through multi-party linkage and multi-case collaboration, identified the balance of interests, guided both parties to reach a settlement, and through negotiation determined technology license fees, providing the right holder with the "positive value" of lawfully collecting technology license fees, replacing the "negative value" of forcible dismantling of infringing equipment, and facilitating the lawful and sustainable use of the involved production equipment.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 237 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC

Article 74, paragraph 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Execution Work of the People's Courts (For Trial Implementation) (Fa Shi [1998] No. 15, revised in 2020)

Articles 1 and 8 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning Enforcement Settlements (Fa Shi [2018] No. 3, revised in 2020)
